{
  "items": [
    {
      "questionId": "q11",
      "maxMarks": 3,
      "marking": {
        "model": "additive",
        "points": [
          {
            "id": "q11_p1",
            "marks": 1,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Maternal deprivation refers to the separation or loss of the mother, or the denial of love and affection from the mother, during the early years of childhood.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["separation", "loss", "mother", "early years", "childhood"],
            "allow": ["loss of mother", "separation from mother", "denial of love/affection", "early childhood"],
            "reject": ["loss of father", "separation from parent (if not specified as mother)", "adolescence"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q11_p2",
            "marks": 1,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "It is a concept developed by John Bowlby.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["Bowlby"],
            "allow": ["Bowlby's theory", "Bowlby's concept"],
            "reject": ["Ainsworth", "Harlow", "Lorenz"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q11_p3",
            "marks": 1,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "It suggests that a lack of maternal care in the first few years of life (e.g., before age 2-3) can lead to long-term psychological, emotional, and social consequences.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["long-term", "consequences", "psychological", "emotional", "social"],
            "allow": ["long-term effects", "negative outcomes", "psychological damage", "emotional problems", "social difficulties"],
            "reject": ["short-term only", "physical consequences only", "no consequences"]
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "questionId": "q12",
      "maxMarks": 16,
      "marking": {
        "model": "additive",
        "points": [
          {
            "id": "q12_p1",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Outline the internal working model (IWM) as proposed by Bowlby.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["internal working model", "Bowlby", "mental representation", "relationship patterns"],
            "allow": ["IWM", "mental model", "template for relationships", "expectations of relationships"],
            "reject": ["attachment styles", "Ainsworth's types"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p2",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Describe Hazan and Shaver's (1987) study on adult attachment styles (secure, anxious-ambivalent, avoidant).",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["Hazan and Shaver", "1987", "secure", "anxious-ambivalent", "avoidant", "adult attachment"],
            "allow": ["Hazan & Shaver", "three attachment styles", "love quiz", "romantic relationships"],
            "reject": ["Ainsworth's Strange Situation", "Bowlby's 44 thieves"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p3",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Outline the findings of Hazan and Shaver's study, e.g., secure adults had positive relationships, avoidant adults were emotionally distant, anxious-ambivalent adults were clingy.",
            "dep": ["q12_p2"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["secure", "positive relationships", "avoidant", "emotionally distant", "anxious-ambivalent", "clingy"],
            "allow": ["secure: trusting, stable", "avoidant: independent, dismissive", "anxious-ambivalent: preoccupied, jealous"],
            "reject": ["incorrect descriptions of styles"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p4",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Describe the longitudinal study by Hazan and Shaver (1990) or the study by Simpson (1990) on how early attachment influences adult relationships.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["longitudinal", "Hazan and Shaver 1990", "Simpson 1990", "early attachment", "adult relationships"],
            "allow": ["follow-up study", "long-term research", "Simpson's study on friendship quality"],
            "reject": ["cross-sectional only", "no mention of early attachment"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p5",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "M",
            "text": "Outline the findings of the longitudinal study, e.g., securely attached infants were more likely to have stable, trusting adult relationships.",
            "dep": ["q12_p4"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["securely attached", "stable", "trusting", "adult relationships"],
            "allow": ["secure infants → positive adult relationships", "avoidant infants → distant relationships", "anxious-ambivalent infants → unstable relationships"],
            "reject": ["no link between early and adult attachment"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p6",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "A",
            "text": "Apply the concept of internal working model to explain how early attachment patterns shape adult relationship expectations and behaviors.",
            "dep": ["q12_p1"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["internal working model", "expectations", "behaviors", "adult relationships"],
            "allow": ["IWM influences how adults form relationships", "template for future relationships", "expectations of partner"],
            "reject": ["no application to adult relationships"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p7",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "A",
            "text": "Apply the findings of Hazan and Shaver to a specific scenario, e.g., how a securely attached adult might handle conflict in a relationship.",
            "dep": ["q12_p2", "q12_p3"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["Hazan and Shaver", "secure", "conflict", "adult relationship"],
            "allow": ["secure adult: open communication, trust", "avoidant adult: withdrawal", "anxious-ambivalent adult: clinginess"],
            "reject": ["no application to scenario"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p8",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "B",
            "text": "Evaluate the research by discussing methodological issues, e.g., Hazan and Shaver's study used a self-report questionnaire (love quiz) which may be subject to social desirability bias.",
            "dep": ["q12_p2"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["methodological", "self-report", "social desirability bias", "questionnaire"],
            "allow": ["subjective responses", "lack of control", "correlation vs causation"],
            "reject": ["no evaluation of methods"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p9",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "B",
            "text": "Evaluate the research by discussing the issue of generalisability, e.g., Hazan and Shaver's sample was predominantly white, middle-class Americans, limiting applicability to other cultures.",
            "dep": ["q12_p2"],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["generalisability", "sample", "white", "middle-class", "American", "culture"],
            "allow": ["cultural bias", "WEIRD sample", "lack of diversity"],
            "reject": ["no mention of generalisability"]
          },
          {
            "id": "q12_p10",
            "marks": 2,
            "code": "B",
            "text": "Evaluate the research by discussing the issue of determinism vs free will, e.g., the theory suggests early attachment determines adult relationships, but individuals can change their attachment style through experience.",
            "dep": [],
            "ft": false,
            "essentialTerms": ["determinism", "free will", "change", "experience", "attachment style"],
            "allow": ["deterministic view", "individual agency", "plasticity of attachment"],
            "reject": ["no discussion of determinism"]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
